note: Positive and defeating cases for contracts/issue-metadata.schema.json. Until this corpus existed the metadata schema was exercised only against the live board, so a change to it could only be judged after it had already reached GitHub. Every case here runs offline from the checkout alone. A defeating case names the substring its refusal must contain, so a case cannot pass by raising some unrelated defect.

cases.proves: A verification engagement pinned to a target pull request and head is a first-class ticket kind.
Adding a kind did not disturb the construction kinds already in the tree.
An engagement must carry its own identity.
An engagement that names no target is not an engagement.
An engagement that does not pin the commit it attacked cannot be reproduced.
An abbreviated head is ambiguous across a growing history.
A verification engagement builds nothing, so a stub identity on it is refused outright rather than admitted unchecked. This is the exact defect that #57 exposed.
Naming an engagement STUB- would reintroduce the construction vocabulary the kind exists to separate.
The new branch did not weaken the conditional already governing implementation stubs.
The kind enum stays closed; a fifth kind must be declared, not asserted by a ticket.
A told story - one actor in one role, one counter, what they expected, what they found, and what they ask of the substrate - is a first-class ticket kind.

cases.proves: A work item can carry a product referent: the canonical capability identifiers it serves, so an expenditure can resolve upward to the intention that justified it. The ticket points at what the repository already names and carries no second definition of it.
A referent that is not shaped like a capability identifier cannot resolve against the projection, so it is refused at the shape rather than silently failing to join later.
One work item names a capability once. Repeating it would let a naive reader count the same work twice, which is the double-counting the attribution rules exist to refuse.
Work that retires a repository surface is a first-class kind: it names the surface it acts on and may be held on a decision, while closing nothing.
A chore must carry its own identity rather than borrowing a construction one.
A chore that does not name its surface cannot be judged done.
A chore builds nothing, so a stub identity on it is a mislabelled build.
A chore discharges no obligation. A surface whose removal leaves a bit unclosed is a demotion of the stub that closed it, not housekeeping.
A chore attacks nothing; the engagement prefix is not available to it.
